title: Basil, from the basics to the details
text:
Basil needs at least 6 hours of direct sun a day, and fewer hours give small, pale leaves.
Pinch off the flower buds as soon as they appear: once basil flowers, its leaves turn bitter and the plant makes fewer new ones.
Harvest from the top, cutting just above a pair of leaves, and two new stems will grow from that point.
A 10 cm cutting placed in a glass of water grows roots in about 7 to 10 days.
Basil leaves turn black when the night drops below 10°C, and the damage does not recover.
Cut basil kept in the fridge turns black within a day, and it keeps longer in a glass of water on the counter.
Basil seeds swell and form a clear gel within minutes in water, which is why some countries add them to drinks.
The smell comes from oils in tiny glands on the leaf surface, which is why a crushed leaf smells stronger than a whole one.
